activities.summary: The views from Sutton Bank are some of the finest in Yorkshire (in fact, according to James Herriot, they’re the finest in England). What better reason to get your car into a low gear and climb the bank up to Sutton Bank National Park Centre? As well as a selection of walking trails, including a family-friendly one that takes in the White Horse at Kilburn, there are cycling options too. Take your own bikes or hire them from Sutton Bank Bikes. The Visitor Centre has a cafe, loos, a natural play area, picnic tables, a shop and helpful staff who will point you in the right direction. Just pay to park. Visitor details – Sutton Bank National Park Centre, Sutton Bank, Thirsk YO7 2EH; 01845 597426

Flat paths and a choice of trails mean that there’s something for families with children of all ages. Kingfishers, herons and bitterness all call Fairburn Ings home, so why not take your binoculars? Good to know – Admission is free, just pay to park (£4). Good to know – This is a brilliant way to get a different perspective on the city, but it’s better suited to older children. It can get crowded during peak visitor months, so perhaps try an early morning stroll for a more relaxing experience. There are some sections that don’t have railings, so it’s best for children who can be trusted to walk safely
